title: Fern-leaved Beech: Cut-leaved Beeches You Can Visit
meta_description: A beech whose leaves come out slashed like a fern. Vienna's in the Rathauspark is the thickest of the park's 449 registered trees.
intro: Genoa's city hall has a beech in its courtyard and its leaves are wrong. They come out narrow and deeply slashed, closer to a fern frond than to the broad oval a beech is supposed to carry, which is the whole of the fern-leaved beech and the only reason anyone notices one. None can be very old. The form was not around before about 1804 and cannot be relied on to come true from seed, so every specimen is a cutting off another one. Leiden's, planted in the Hortus in 1818, is the oldest in the Netherlands and has grown outward into one enormous low dome. Vienna's, planted in 1873, is six metres round, the thickest of the 449 trees registered in the Rathauspark. Munich registers its two not for size or age but for how rarely the form turns up anywhere in the city.
